payload.claim: Criterion 4's dedicated witness (`test_a_probe_only_a_test_the_diff_did_not_add_notices_is_rebutted_with_that_failure_recorded`, tests/test_session.py:3690) is supposed to prove `base_results` comes from the task's pre-turn baseline and not from `latest.results` (its own docstring says 'An attempt's suite stands in for neither side'). But it reuses the shared `_TASK_HEAD` fixture (collected=["t.py::test_old","t.py::test_a"]) for the attempt suite, and this test's probe-cell baseline collects ["t.py::test_old","t.py::test_added","t.py::test_new"] — none of which overlaps with the extra name "t.py::test_a" in `_TASK_HEAD`. So `added_tests(_TASK_BASE, probe_baseline)` and `added_tests(_TASK_HEAD, probe_baseline)` compute the identical set {test_added, test_new}, and every assertion in the test passes unchanged. Replacing `base_results=baseline.results` with `base_results=latest.results` at this line keeps this specific witness green while reintroducing exactly the wrong version the task's notes name as one that must be killed. (Three other tests reusing the same fixtures with `t.py::test_a` as the probed failure do catch this regression, so the overall suite is not blind to it, but the test filed specifically to prove criterion 4's base-vs-latest requirement does not.)
